mappings.note: Picks the equation that is saponification. LO-8 names saponification explicitly.
Names given compounds. Nomenclature within a homologous series, LO-4.
Ethanoic acid plus the alcohol that oxidises back to it, giving an ester -- esterification, LO-8. Structures are also demanded, which is C 1.3-LO-4.
Why detergents outperform soaps, especially in hard water. The soap/detergent distinction of LO-9.
Identifies functional groups in given compounds. LO-4 verbatim.
Ethene from ethanol by dehydration, with the equation. A reaction of ethanol, LO-8.

Toxicity of methanol. LO-8 is written for ethanol and ethanoic acid only, and methanol is neither, so the C 1.2 competency on the nature and properties of substances is cited rather than stretching the outcome.
Ethanol with sodium: name the gas, balance the equation. A reaction of ethanol, LO-8.
Role of conc. H2SO4 in dehydrating ethanol at 443 K, with the equation. A reaction of ethanol, LO-8.
Carbon forming compounds with chlorine and with oxygen. Its ability to bond with many elements is the tetravalency of LO-3; the group numbers are only scaffolding.
Configuration of chlorine and the electron dot structure of Cl2. Chlorine is not a carbon compound, so C 1.3-LO-4 does not apply and the competency is cited.
Compares catenation in carbon and silicon with reasons. LO-3's catenation clause.
Test distinguishing ethane from ethene. The verdict is which homologous series each belongs to (saturated versus unsaturated), LO-4.
Matches reactions to their names (addition, substitution, and so on). Reaction typing has no outcome in this frame; cited at the C 1.3 competency.
What the reagents written over the arrows do -- catalysts and oxidising agents. Equation notation, the C 1.3 competency; no LO covers it.
Ethanoic acid with sodium hydrogencarbonate: the salt, the gas, an apparatus to prove it, and the equation. A reaction of ethanoic acid, LO-8.
Hydrocarbons, functional groups and homologous families are LO-4 of C 1.1; the demand for the STRUCTURAL difference between saturated and unsaturated, with examples drawn, is C 1.3-LO-4.
Names and explains hydrogenation of vegetable oils. An addition reaction, which has no learning outcome here; cited at C 1.3.
Two unrelated parts: the electron dot structure of CCl4 (C 1.3-LO-4) and the definition and equation of saponification (LO-8).
Design an activity to prepare an ester, with diagram and reaction. Esterification, LO-8.
Chain identifying ethanoic acid, sodium ethanoate, the alcohol and the ester, covering both esterification and its reversal by alkali. LO-8 names both reactions.
Lime-water test on the gas from ethanoic acid, and whether ethanol would behave the same. Contrasts the two compounds LO-8 names.
Ethanol to ethene, and the oxidation to ethanoic acid. Both are LO-8 reactions. (Part (b) is written 'methanol to ethanoic acid', which cannot be right -- see defect list.)
Draws the isomers of C3H6O and their electron dot structures. LO-4 verbatim, both clauses.
Five reaction types with examples. Hydrogenation, oxidation, substitution and combustion have no outcome here and go to the C 1.3 competency; saponification is named in LO-8, so that is cited too.
Ethanol dehydrated to ethene, then hydrogenated to ethane, confirmed by combustion stoichiometry. The first step is an ethanol reaction (LO-8); the addition and combustion steps sit at C 1.3.
Yellow burner flame from blocked holes -- incomplete combustion. No combustion outcome exists in this frame; cited at C 1.3.
Sudden loss of vision after drinking spirit -- methanol poisoning. As with 85376, LO-8 covers only ethanol and ethanoic acid, so the competency is cited.
Bromine water, not chlorine water, is the unsaturation test; ethene decolourises it. Identifying the unsaturated series is LO-4, and the equation for the addition is C 1.3.
Vanaspati and ghee versus vegetable oil -- saturated versus unsaturated fats. Series identification, LO-4; no equation or structure is asked for.
Ethanol as solvent and intoxicant, and whether production should be banned. Value-based with little chemistry, but ethanol's uses and effects are the LO-8 slot; nothing finer exists.
Which acid pickles contain (ethanoic acid), inside a value-based stem. The only chemistry demand is a property/occurrence of ethanoic acid, LO-8.
'What is an alcohol' is the -OH family, LO-4; the rest concerns ethanol in cough syrup and its misuse, which falls to LO-8.
Carbon and hydrogen as the essential constituents of organic compounds. The carbon-centred basis of LO-3.
Valency of carbon is four. Tetravalency, LO-3.
Why organic compounds are so numerous -- catenation and tetravalency. LO-3 restated.
What all members of a family share -- the functional group and a general formula. Homologous series, LO-4.
The '-al' suffix marks aldehydes. Functional group and naming, LO-4.
Aldehyde is the terminal group, ketone the internal one. Functional-group identification, LO-4.
Why a candle flame is yellow -- glowing unburnt carbon from incomplete combustion. Combustion has no outcome here; cited at C 1.3.
CnH2n is the alkene family and is unsaturated. General formula and series, LO-4.
A compound smelling of vinegar is ethanoic acid. A property of ethanoic acid, LO-8.
Ethanoic acid with ethanol over conc. H2SO4 gives an ester. Esterification, LO-8.
Names the second alkyne (propyne) -- LO-4 of C 1.1 -- and also asks for its structure, which is C 1.3-LO-4.
Bromine decolourised, so the hydrocarbon is unsaturated. Series identification, LO-4.
Test for ethanoic acid (litmus, or fizzing with hydrogencarbonate). A property of ethanoic acid, LO-8.
Groundnut oil is the unsaturated one. Saturated versus unsaturated, LO-4.
What soap does when clothes are washed. Cleansing action, LO-9.
Methanol added to make denatured spirit. The subject is ethanol and how it is made undrinkable -- a property/use of ethanol, LO-8.
Whether a detergent can reveal hard water. The soap/detergent distinction, LO-9 -- a duplicate of 85321 (see defect list).
When a burner gives yellow soot -- insufficient air, incomplete combustion. Cited at C 1.3 for want of a combustion outcome.
IUPAC and common names of a ketone and an acid. Naming from the functional group, LO-4.
Which formulae share a homologous series. LO-4 verbatim.
Which formula carries a triple bond, i.e. which is an alkyne. Series membership from the general formula, LO-4.
Formula of butene given butane. Moving between homologous series by their general formulae, LO-4.
C2H6O used as a fuel is ethanol. Identity and use of ethanol, LO-8.
What methanol and ethanol share -- the -OH group. Functional-group identification, LO-4; nothing is drawn, so not C 1.3-LO-4.
Functional groups of alcohols, aldehydes and carboxylic acids. LO-4 verbatim.
Which of four formulae add, with justification -- C3H4 and C2H4 are unsaturated. Series identification, LO-4.
Which element catenates most and why (carbon, strong C-C bonds). LO-3's catenation clause.
